To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an attention-based deep net for learning to rank outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in image retrieval and text query tasks.
the proposed attention-based deep net outperforms the existing state-of-the-art models in learning to rank.

our model achieves a 3.5% increase in the mean average precision over the state of the art in the image retrieval data set, and a 3.3% increase in the normalized discounted cumulative gain in the text data set.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions:
the following questions. How can we use neural networks to learn to rank? What is the effect of different types of embeddings? What is the performance of our model in image retrieval tasks?

the following questions: 1) How can attention be incorporated into a neural network for learning to rank? 2) How can the embeddings of the search results and queries be learned? 3) How can a neural network be trained in a listwise manner to learn the ranking of search results?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is able to achieve a better performance than other models in learning to rank.
our proposed attention-based deep network outperforms other deep neural networks and traditional ranking methods in both the text and image retrieval data sets.
the proposed model outperforms the baseline model in both the image and text data sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the attention mechanism can help to learn the importance of each embedding in the model, and the decoder mechanism can help to improve the performance of the model.
the attention mechanism can be used in the ranking model to learn the relative importance between queries and search results.

we propose an attention mechanism for learning the importance of different parts of the queries and the search results, and then we apply a decoder mechanism to generate the ranks of the results in a list-wise manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attention-based deep learning can be used in ranking systems.
the attention mechanism and the decoder are effective at learning the ranking function for search results.
the attention-based model outperforms other models in both cases.
